A statement such as `server.close;` or `count === 0;` computes a value and does nothing with it. Usually it is a mistake: the parentheses of a call are missing, or `===` was typed where `=` was meant.

Calls, `new`, assignments, `await`, `yield`, `delete`, `void`, `i++`, and directives such as `"use strict"` do something, so they are not reported.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```js
server.close;
count === 0;
`Hello, ${name}`;
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
"use strict";

server.close();
count = 0;
console.log(`Hello, ${name}`);
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowShortCircuit` | `false` | Allow `a && b()`, `a \|\| b()` and `a ?? b()`, if the right side would be allowed as a statement. |
| `allowTernary` | `false` | Allow `a ? b() : c()`, if both branches would be allowed as statements. |
| `allowTaggedTemplates` | `false` | Allow a tagged template as a statement. |
| `enforceForJSX` | `false` | Also report a JSX element as a statement. |
| `ignoreDirectives` | `false` | Allow strings at the start of a file or a function when `ecmaVersion` is 3, which has no directives. |

By default, `&&` in place of an `if` is reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
isReady && start();
```

{/* good {"options": [{"allowShortCircuit": true}]} */}
```js
isReady && start();
```

The right side still has to do something:

{/* bad {"options": [{"allowShortCircuit": true}]} */}
```js
isReady && start;
```

{/* good {"options": [{"allowTernary": true}]} */}
```js
isReady ? start() : wait();
```

A tag is a function, so a tagged template can have an effect:

{/* good {"options": [{"allowTaggedTemplates": true}]} */}
```js
sql`DELETE FROM sessions`;
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"enforceForJSX": true}]} */}
```jsx
<Spinner />;
```
